title: Linux IPv4 TCP use-after-free can permit remote code execution
summary: The IPv4 TCP connection setup flaw can lead to remote code execution. Ubuntu describes an unreleased exploit using MPTCP and warns that the underlying flaw is not specific to MPTCP.

severity.rationale: Remote kernel code execution threatens developer and agent hosts accepting network connections. No public or in-the-wild exploit claim is established here.

affected.note: Affected branches require distribution-specific backports. Ubuntu 22.04 LTS and newer have archive fixes. USN-9170-1 documents broad Ubuntu Pro fix availability for Ubuntu 20.04 LTS and 18.04 LTS, including generic and cloud flavors; USN-9170-4 adds Azure FIPS and Azure 5.4 fixes. The November 9 bulletin still lists 20.04 and older as pending. Current 16.04 fix availability is unconfirmed here.
USN-9027-2 lists linux-image-5.15.0-203-fips at this package version through Ubuntu Pro FIPS Updates. This is not a generic upstream kernel threshold.
USN-9170-4 lists linux-image-5.4.0-1174-azure-fips at this package version through Ubuntu Pro FIPS Updates.
USN-9170-4 lists linux-image-5.4.0-1174-azure at this package version through Ubuntu Pro.
USN-9192-1 lists linux-image-6.8.0-1068-nvidia and linux-image-6.8.0-1068-nvidia-64k at this package version. These package thresholds do not apply to other kernel flavors.

exposure: Relevant to exposed IPv4 TCP handling. Disabling MPTCP alone is not a complete fix for the underlying vulnerability.

params.instructions: Identify the running kernel, distribution release and kernel flavor; compare the exact package with the vendor CVE tracker and update channel.

remediation.details: Install the fixed package for the exact distribution release and kernel flavor, then reboot. Ubuntu 22.04 LTS and newer have archive fixes; enabling -proposed is unnecessary. For Ubuntu 20.04 and 18.04, use the Ubuntu Pro package mappings in USN-9170-1, supplemented by USN-9170-4 for Azure FIPS and Azure 5.4. FIPS Updates require the matching channel. USN-9192-1 lists the Ubuntu 22.04 NVIDIA 6.8 fix. The November 9 bulletin predates these older-release notices; current Ubuntu 16.04 availability is unconfirmed here, so check the vendor CVE tracker.
remediation.risk: Medium. Reboot interrupts workloads; kernel ABI changes can require rebuilding third-party modules.

verification: Confirm the running kernel after reboot matches a vendor-confirmed fixed package for the exact kernel flavor.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.
